rallied to 94.8050 per dollar, its highest since July 1, defying a selloff in Asian currencies triggered by rising U.S. Treasury yields. Higher oil prices also presented little hurdle, with the rupee slicing through the 94.90-95.00 resistance area.

Traders said foreign banks were offering dollars for flows whose source was not immediately clear. They pointed out that daily fixing was at a discount, indicating interest in selling dollars at the Reserve Bank of India reference rate.

The RBI, meanwhile, was selling dollars heavily through state-run banks, traders said. One trader said volume on the day had been particularly large, helping the rupee rally despite an unfavourable backdrop for Asian currencies.

U.S. Treasury yields weighed on regional currencies, with that on the 10-year climbing to its highest in about one-and-a-half years. Traders ramped up bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike at this month's meeting amid inflation concerns. The odds of a rate increase at the September 15-16 meeting are now being priced at nearly 70%.
Rate-hike expectations have grown along with rising oil prices following the resumption of fighting between the United States and Iran.

Meanwhile, the RBI's heavy currency intervention has contributed to increased market focus on its ballooning FX forward book. The central bank's dollar forward positions hit an all-time high of $137 billion in July, a period in which it offered swaps for FCNR(B) deposits raised by banks.
